converter.defaultDescription: Choose the quantity and the units of the reading.

converter.footnoteTorque: Check lbf·in against lbf·ft: they differ by a factor of 12. The applicable task sets the torque value.
converter.footnoteUnits: The source unit must always match your instrument or documentation.
converter.formula: Result = value × source factor / target factor. Absolute temperatures include the scale offset. Ranges are converted at both ends.
converter.formulaTorque: 120 lbf·in = 10 lbf·ft ≈ 13.5581794833 N·m. It does not compute preload, select a torque or correct for adapters.
converter.torqueNoticeTitle: A mathematical conversion, not a torque specification
converter.torqueNotice: This result only converts units. The torque value, its tolerance, the sequence and any adapter or extension correction come from the approved maintenance data for the task (AMM, SRM, CMM or other authorised documentation). It does not replace that documentation or the check with a calibrated tool.
converter.copyTorqueNote: unit conversion only; the torque value comes from the approved maintenance data

torque.label: Torque
torque.description: Converts the torque given in the task. It does not determine how tight a fastener should be.

length.label: Length
length.description: Accepts fractions such as 3/16 or 1 3/16. Mil/thou means one thousandth of an inch.

mass.label: Mass
mass.description: lb and oz are units of mass; lbf belongs to Force.

volume.label: Volume
volume.description: US gallons and Imperial gallons are not equivalent. Choose the system on the receipt.

density.label: Density
density.description: Keep the same temperature basis. This conversion does not correct for thermal expansion.

pressure.label: Pressure
pressure.description: The conversion keeps the absolute or gauge reference of the reading.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.description: Absolute temperature: includes the scale offset. For increments use Temperature difference.

temperatureDelta.label: Temperature difference
temperatureDelta.description: An increase of 20 °C equals 36 °F; 32 is not added.

force.label: Force
force.description: Does not convert mass into force or estimate preload from a torque.

flowVolume.label: Volume flow
flowVolume.description: Mass flow also needs a density; this only converts volume/time.

distance.label: Distance
distance.description: NM is the nautical mile; N·m is torque and nm is the nanometre.
